items.title: Ellen Rowe interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, December 2, 2024
items.q: I’m going to read a quote from Karolina Strassmayer.

ctx.x: Yes. I was, yeah. I think about this a lot. There’s a wonderful younger writer who, you know none of us could have an undergraduate jazz major at the time because there wasn’t one. There was a master’s degree which is why I stayed on. But a wonderful composer/arranger Shari Feder who is there. She went more the jingles and commercial music route. She was a couple of years behind me. And of course Maria came in a year after me. And there were some really good, you know, players there. I know I’m going to be…

How do you feel about the state of women in jazz right now? I’m going to read a quote from Karolina Strassmayer. She was talking about the expectations of a woman and “How can I embody the spirit of jazz if I’m concerned whether people like me or they think that I’m pretty or they think that I’m nice. So I found that there’s a contradiction between my socialization as a girl, as a woman, and the music I play.”

Well of course needless to say I think about this constantly, you know especially with trying to get a lot of young women in our program which we’ve been, I’ll say I’ve been pretty good at. I think we have nine or ten women in our program of 55 students, and that’s without a jazz vocal program, so these are all instrumentalists. Yeah I think that’s an ongoing concern for younger women. I think it’s less of a concern than it was 30, 40 years ago. I see a lot of my younger women students are just really gung-ho and…
